clue.text: Supplement to produce litter

parts.note: to pup is to give birth to a litter of puppies

explanation.surface: An instruction for feeding a breeding dog or cat: a supplement to help produce a litter.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra amount added to bring something back to full is a supplement.

clue.text: High water that runs in odd places

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words that runs are taken

explanation.surface: A description of a mountain stream running down from on high.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, water found high up in the hills.

clue.text: Poster about one Glaswegian golf club perhaps

indicators.note: the poster's letters go round the others, as if surrounding them

yin is the Scots word for one, as said in Glasgow

explanation.surface: A sign about a Glasgow golfer or golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Club is not a golf club but one of the four suits in a pack of cards; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is one example of a card in a standard pack, the suit marked with a trefoil.

clue.text: Spoil marks in exam

indicators.note: the letter for marks is placed inside the exam word

parts.note: an exam paper, or simply a paper
M is short for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A complaint that a student's exam was spoilt by marking.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil a person is to indulge them too much, to coddle them.

clue.text: Car-mad character's device that may be lethal

parts.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is obsessed with motor cars; with the possessive, Toad's
a tool is a device

explanation.surface: A dangerous gadget belonging to someone obsessed with cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad, from Kenneth Grahame's children's novel The Wind in the Willows, is famously crazy about motor cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Many poisonous fungi go by this name, and eating one can kill you.

clue.text: Record short reindeer, one shod with metal bits

indicators.note: the word for record loses its last letter, cut short

parts.note: to tape is to record
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: Put a little reindeer on record, perhaps one with metal shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoofers in this style wear shoes fitted with metal plates on heel and toe.

clue.text: Turn away very briefly at stores

indicators.note: the word at holds the other letters inside it, as a store holds goods
the word very is shortened by dropping its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Someone turning away for a moment while at the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert your eyes or gaze is to turn them aside.

clue.text: Like 78 yachts at sea rounding Costa Rica

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters go round the abbreviation, as a yacht rounds a cape

parts.note: CR is the international code for Costa Rica

explanation.surface: Seventy-eight yachts sailing round the coast of Costa Rica.
explanation.walkthrough: The 78 is not a number of boats but an old 78 rpm gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: Old shellac gramophone discs played at 78 rpm are notorious for their crackly, hissing sound.

clue.text: Operating drug unit

parts.note: a machine that is on is operating
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A hospital ward where drugs are administered during surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number at the base of counting.

clue.text: Hedonist left swimmer downing posh drink

indicators.note: the swimmer swallows the other letters, as if downing a drink

parts.note: an otter is a swimming animal
U means upper-class, posh
the drink is crossword slang for the sea

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker has left a swimmer gulping a fancy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey the lotophagi lived in idle bliss, so the term means someone given over to pleasure and indolence.

clue.text: Travellers quietly hide commercial guide for other ones

indicators.note: the travellers' word conceals the commercial inside it

parts.note: the Roma are a travelling people
an ad is a commercial
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Travellers quietly hiding an advert that guides other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other ones' refers back to Travellers: a map is a guide for travellers of a different kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist or traveller uses a chart of highways to find the way.

clue.text: Serious eastern novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of eastern are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grave book from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere and solemn in intent is serious, not joking.

clue.text: I demand some oomph among naturists — and boobs

indicators.note: the demand and oomph go into the middle of the naturists' word

parts.note: naturists go about as nudes
to exact is to demand
it is sex appeal, oomph

explanation.definitionFit: Boobs are mistakes or errors, and these are inaccuracies; 'terminological inexactitude' is a famous euphemism for a lie.

clue.text: Complex score ended with C, fading gradually

indicators.note: complex means intricate or knotted, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A musical score that finishes on the note C, dying away.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this direction means getting gradually softer, fading away.

clue.text: Gee them up possibly in June mostly to start early

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the shortened month
most of the month's name, its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: gee is the spoken name of the letter G

explanation.surface: Encouraging people in June, perhaps to get going early.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from athletics: a runner who leaves before the starting pistol has started too soon.

clue.text: River engulfs grand drive

indicators.note: the river swallows up the letter for grand

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A river swallowing up a grand driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a strong inner impulse or desire, as is an urge.

clue.text: One dance, three drinks

definitions.meaning: a Cuban ballroom dance named for its triple step
cha is slang for tea, so three cups of it are cha three times over

explanation.surface: An evening out: one dance and three drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is old British slang for tea, from the Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin American ballroom dance from Cuba, named for the rhythm of its steps.

clue.text: Awful amateur threesome, our lot lugging old clubs

indicators.note: the threesome carries the other letters within it

parts.note: a trio is a threesome
C is short for clubs, the card suit
our lot means us

clue.text: Former ruler twice hires apprentice hawk handler

indicators.note: the former word takes on the apprentice inside it

parts.note: past means former

indicators.note: the ruler's letters appear two times

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, a ruler

explanation.walkthrough: A hawk is not a bird here but a plasterer's square board for holding plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer's hawk is the flat board held in one hand to carry plaster, so the tradesman handles one.

clue.text: Told fancied player to give up

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a seed is a fancied player in a tennis draw

explanation.surface: A favourite player is told to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or surrender something, such as territory, is to give it up.

clue.text: Plod right to wrap up drug case

indicators.note: the right word encloses the letters, wrapping them

parts.note: true means right, correct

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: Plod looks like British slang for a policeman, fitting the drug case; it is the verb for walking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk slowly and heavily, as one does when weary.

clue.text: He and I'd correctly rigged current type

indicators.note: rigged means arranged dishonestly, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Two people boasting they wired something up properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity generated by water turning turbines is one kind of current.

clue.text: Scoop! Foreign articles about duke

indicators.note: the two articles go around the duke

parts.note: la and le are French words for the

explanation.surface: A newspaper exclusive: foreign reports about a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoop! looks like a news exclusive, fitting articles; it is a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled deep spoon for serving soup is a kind of scoop.

clue.text: Anonymous solitary plant

indicators.note: anonymous means without a name, so N for name is removed

parts.note: alone means solitary

explanation.surface: A single unnamed plant growing on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A succulent with fleshy leaves whose sap is used to soothe burns.

clue.text: Scrap wheels, old, given space at home?

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
aged means old

clue.text: Dispute two or three abbreviations in cricket

definitions.text: two or three abbreviations in cricket
definitions.meaning: R for runs, O for overs and W for wickets are cricket scoring abbreviations, three letters in a line

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game; its scorecards use R for runs, O for overs and W for wickets.

clue.text: Eg second line installed for railway in common

parts.note: ordinary means common, everyday

clue.text: Cornish port docked days for honeymoon couple

parts.note: Newlyn is a fishing port in Cornwall

explanation.walkthrough: Newlyn is a fishing harbour near Penzance in Cornwall, England's south-western tip.

clue.text: Call up the day before to collect fine

indicators.note: the day before gathers the fine word into its middle

parts.note: eve is the day before an event
OK means fine
